commits.message:
A holder that sets its own rows settles them, and one that splices rows fills them first (rich-control-codes-xh4n.yws)

Review of #593: a Tree's root label and a Syntax line moved to the right
edge under a filler; a change between two right-to-left texts and a row
under an open overlay lost their place mid-transition; the caret was found
before the leading fill. Tree and Syntax settle their rows, ChangeFrame and
WidgetApp fill before splicing, paint finds the caret on the placed row,
and leadingFill walks a row once without allocating.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

A right-to-left row says where it stands on the frame, and whoever fills the row places it, so no option travels to tell text (rich-control-codes-xh4n.yws)

Text stamps an unplaced right-to-left row with Style.edge (the row and the
width it was laid out in); Segment.leadingFill is the one reader, and Padding,
Layout, Viewport, scroll, Console.print and paint's frame fit read it.
PASSES_EDGE, passingOptions, fillingOptions, renderFilling and renderPassing
are deleted, so a user's own wrapper hands the row on with nothing to know.
Pretty, JSON, Traceback and the strips set their own lines (Segment.settled).

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
foreground-muted's per-ground floor reads the one disabledInk textOn draws; the ordering is tested with its margin beside the 3:1 floor (rich-unfiled-791c.tofk)
foreground-muted is ordered against the disabled text textOn draws, and held no stronger than foreground (rich-unfiled-791c.tofk)
foreground-muted is held past foreground-disabled on every ground it is held on, derived and authored alike (rich-unfiled-791c.tofk)
A derived palette's foreground-muted reads stronger than its foreground-disabled, on every bundled base (rich-unfiled-791c.tofk)

decodeAnsi reads each escape's meaning off the lexer's one parse (rich-control-codes-xh4n.7c0) (#591)

* decodeAnsi reads each escape's meaning off the lexer's one parse, so the CSI and escape grammar is defined once (rich-control-codes-xh4n.7c0)

A sequence lexeme carries its introducer kind, parameters, intermediates and
final byte, and sequenceToken dispatches on those fields; ESCAPES' CSI and
escape alternatives and SEQUENCE_BREAK are gone, and the text regex keeps only
what text does. The lexer reads ground text, collected bytes and string
payloads in sticky runs, and drawLine builds its text regex once per line with
no generator per lexeme.

Bench (/tmp/probe590/bench.ts, interleaved min of 15, vs master at 0.30.0):
SGR decode 376 vs 416 ms, scan 234 vs 272; plain decode 266 vs 365, scan 66 vs 182.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Review: one intermediate range, one count reader, a CSI with a parameter after an intermediate is undrawn, and the text scan owns its cursor (rich-control-codes-xh4n.7c0)

* Review: a CSI and an escape are two lexeme types each read by its own total function, and the no-byte-drawn gate surrounds each sequence with text no final can be (rich-control-codes-xh4n.7c0)
